dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:4901.text: A cloth wrap, 帊. Formed from 巾, with 菐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4902.text: A carriage curtain. Formed from 巾, with 憲 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4903.text: A ceremonial apron. In remote antiquity clothing only covered the front; 巿 depicts this. The Son of Heaven has a vermilion apron, feudal lords a red one, grand officers a green crosspiece. Formed from 巾, depicting an attached belt. All characters in this group are formed from 巿.

shuowen:4904.text: A reddish leather ceremonial apron worn with a scholar-official’s jue-cap ritual costume instead of the higher-rank apron. It was cut into a distinctive four-cornered shape, and its color differed from the wearer’s skirt. Formed from 巿, with 合 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4905.text: Silk fabric. Formed from 巾, with 白 indicating the sound. All characters in this group are formed from 帛.

shuowen:4906.text: Patterned weaving from Xiangyi. Formed from 帛, with 金 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4907.text: The color of the west. When yin governs, things turn white. Formed from 入 joined with 二; 二 is a yin number. All characters in this group are formed from 白.

shuowen:4908.text: The whiteness of the moon. Formed from 白, with 交 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The moon rises white and bright.”

shuowen:4909.text: The whiteness of the sun. Formed from 白, with 堯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4910.text: A person’s complexion white. Formed from 白, with 析 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4911.text: The whiteness of old people. Formed from 白, with 番 indicating the sound. The Changes says: “Adorned, yet white.”

shuowen:4912.text: The whiteness of birds. Formed from 白, with 隺 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4913.text: The whiteness of frost and snow. Formed from 白, with 豈 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4914.text: The whiteness of plant flowers. Formed from 白, with 巴 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4915.text: The whiteness of jade and stone. Formed from 白, with 敫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4916.text: White light seen through a gap. Formed from 白, with small portions visible above and below.

shuowen:4917.text: Manifest or bright. Formed from three 白. Read like 皎.

shuowen:4918.text: Worn-out clothing. Formed from 巾, depicting clothing worn out. All characters in this group are formed from 㡀.

shuowen:4919.text: A cloth, 帗. Another explanation: worn-out clothing. Formed from 攴 and 㡀; 㡀 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:4920.text: Sewing clothing with needle and thread. Formed from 㡀 and abbreviated 丵. All characters in this group are formed from 黹.

shuowen:4921.text: Combining the bright colors of the five hues. Formed from 黹, with 虘 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The garments are brilliantly colored.”

shuowen:4922.text: A pattern alternating white and black. Formed from 黹, with 甫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4923.text: A pattern alternating black and blue-green. Formed from 黹, with 犮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4924.text: Combining silk colors of the five hues. Formed from 黹, with abbreviated 綷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4925.text: Mountains, dragons and pheasants on ceremonial robes: 黺 means painting with powder. Formed from 黹 and abbreviated 粉. This is Wei Hong’s explanation.

shuowen:4926.text: The most precious being endowed by Heaven and Earth. This is the large-seal form, depicting arms and shins. All characters in this group are formed from 人.

shuowen:4927.text: Not yet capped as an adult. Formed from 人, with 童 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4928.text: To nurture. Formed from 人 and abbreviated 𤓽; 𤓽 is ancient-script 孚.

shuowen:4929.text: Affection or closeness. Formed from 人 and 二.

shuowen:4930.text: To raise the heels. Formed from 人, with 止 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4931.text: The span of outstretched arms, one xun: eight chi. Formed from 人, with 刃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4932.text: To learn. Formed from 人 and 士.

shuowen:4933.text: To associate. Formed from 人 and 交.

shuowen:4934.text: Complete or equipped. Formed from 人, with 巽 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4935.text: The appearance of an adorned cap. Formed from 人, with 求 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Caps and robes, well adorned.”

shuowen:4936.text: A pendant on the great belt. Formed from 人, 凡 and 巾. A pendant must have a cloth, called its ornament.

shuowen:4937.text: Gentle; a designation for learned practitioners. Formed from 人, with 需 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4938.text: Having the talent of a thousand people. Formed from 人, with 夋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4939.text: Proud. Formed from 人, with 桀 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4940.text: A surname. Formed from 人, with 軍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4941.text: A personal name. Formed from 人, with 及 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4942.text: A personal name. Formed from 人, with 亢 indicating the sound. The Analects mentions Chen Kang, 陳伉.

shuowen:4943.text: Senior or eldest. Formed from 人, with 白 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4944.text: Middle. Formed from 人 and 中; 中 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:4945.text: Yin’s sage minister Aheng, who governed all under Heaven. Formed from 人 and 尹.

shuowen:4946.text: A son of the Gaoxin ruler, Yao’s Minister of Education and ancestor of Yin. Formed from 人, with 契 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4947.text: A person’s courtesy name. Formed from 人, with 青 indicating the sound. Eastern Qi calls a son-in-law 倩.

shuowen:4948.text: A female official. Formed from 人, with 予 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4949.text: Intent extending to the multitude. Formed from 人, with 公 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4950.text: Clever. Formed from 人, with 瞏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4951.text: At peace. Formed from 人, with 炎 indicating the sound. Read like 談.

shuowen:4952.text: Swift. Formed from 人, with 旬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4953.text: Unsettled. Formed from 人, with 容 indicating the sound. Another explanation: splendid.

shuowen:4954.text: Between Song and Wei, splendor is called 僷僷. Formed from 人, with 葉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4955.text: Good. Formed from 人, with 圭 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4956.text: 奇侅, extraordinary. Formed from 人, with 亥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4957.text: Remarkable. Formed from 人, with 鬼 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: “Great marvels and anomalies.”

shuowen:4958.text: Extraordinary. Formed from 人, with 韋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4959.text: Natural substance and cultivated refinement blended harmoniously. Formed from 人, with 分 indicating the sound. The Analects says: “Refinement and substance in balanced harmony.” [The received gloss 文質僣 has a textual variant; Duan interprets it as intermingling.]

shuowen:4960.text: A pleasing appearance. Formed from 人, with 尞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4961.text: Dignified bearing. Formed from 人, with 必 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Their bearing is dignified.”

shuowen:4962.text: Complete. Formed from 人, with 孨 indicating the sound. Read like the 𣹏 River in Runan. The Book of Yu says: “Seek widely for complete achievement.”

shuowen:4963.text: Tall and strong, 儠巤. Formed from 人, with 巤 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “Let a tall and strong man assist him.”

shuowen:4964.text: A manner of walking. Formed from 人, with 麃 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Travelers walk in crowds.”

shuowen:4965.text: The measured pace of a walker. Formed from 人, with 難 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The measured movement of the jade pendants.”

shuowen:4966.text: A compliant or winding appearance. Formed from 人, with 委 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The Zhou road winds gently.”

shuowen:4967.text: Refined or practiced. Formed from 人, with 貴 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a tall appearance.

shuowen:4968.text: High. Formed from 人, with 喬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4969.text: Large. Formed from 人, with 矣 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Strong and grand.”

shuowen:4970.text: A large appearance. Formed from 人, with 同 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The spirits were not grieved.”

shuowen:4971.text: Upright. Formed from 人, with 吉 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Both sturdy and trained.”

shuowen:4972.text: Large. Formed from 人, with 吳 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The great man is grand.”

shuowen:4973.text: A large belly. Formed from 人, with 工 indicating the sound. Read like 紅.

shuowen:4974.text: Rapid or swift. Formed from 人, with 單 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou says that hooked weapons should not be too quick or springy in action.

shuowen:4975.text: Strong or a match for another. Formed from 人, with 建 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4976.text: Strong. Formed from 人, with 京 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4977.text: Arrogant. Formed from 人, with 敖 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4978.text: Brave and strong. Formed from 人, with 气 indicating the sound. The Book of Zhou says: “Stalwart brave men.”

shuowen:4979.text: Disrespectful. Formed from 人, with 居 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4980.text: To raise the head. Formed from 人, with 嚴 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a pleasing appearance.

shuowen:4981.text: A pleasing appearance. Formed from 人, with 參 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4982.text: To rely upon or get by, 聊. Formed from 人, with 里 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4983.text: A large appearance. Formed from 人, with 半 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4984.text: Large. Formed from 人, with 奄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4985.text: A martial appearance. Formed from 人, with 閒 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Solemn and martial.”

shuowen:4986.text: Having strength. Formed from 人, with 丕 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “With carts, powerfully.”

shuowen:4987.text: Strong and forceful. Formed from 人, with 思 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “That man is handsome and strong.”

shuowen:4988.text: Prominent and great. Formed from 人, with 㔬 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Prominent is that Milky Way.”

shuowen:4989.text: A tall appearance. Another explanation: touching the ground. Another: to replace. Formed from 人, with 廷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4990.text: To assist. Formed from 人, with 朋 indicating the sound. Read like 陪 in 陪位.

shuowen:4991.text: Blazing and flourishing. Formed from 人, with 扇 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The beautiful wife, in full power, occupies her place.”

shuowen:4992.text: To warn. Formed from 人, with 敬 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “Put the palace on guard.”

shuowen:4993.text: Good. Formed from 人, with 叔 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “A good ending has a good beginning.” Another explanation: beginning.

shuowen:4994.text: Even and straight. Formed from 人, with 庸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4995.text: Indistinctly perceived. Formed from 人, with 愛 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Dimly felt, yet not seen.”

shuowen:4996.text: Similar to one another. Formed from 人, with 方 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4997.text: Not seeing clearly. Formed from 人, with 弗 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4998.text: A sound. Formed from 人, with 悉 indicating the sound. Read like 㞕.

shuowen:4999.text: Exact and careful. Formed from 人, with 幾 indicating the sound. The Bright Hall Monthly Ordinances says: “The count is about to reach its precise end.”

shuowen:5000.text: To carry a load. Formed from 人, with 它 indicating the sound.
